name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Courtney's incumbency in a D+4 district with a history of double-digit wins
Dominant fundraising edge: $603k cash on hand vs. $125k for Austin
Prediction markets price Courtney near 97% to win
No public polling, but no signs of a competitive race or outside investment against Courtney
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's Democratic lean, Courtney's incumbency, his roughly five-to-one cash advantage, and markets pricing his win odds near 97% all support a comfortable margin, and nothing in the evidence suggests a meaningful challenge.
model.watch: A surge in challenger fundraising or late outside spending against Courtney, combined with a sharply worse national environment for Democrats, would be the main route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joe Courtney, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in Connecticut's eastern district, which leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding more than $600,000 on hand after raising over $760,000, while Republican George Austin has raised roughly $314,000 with about $125,000 available. Little outside money is engaged on either side.

No public polls of the race are available, and national ratings organizations have not weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the resource gap. Prediction markets give Courtney roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent well funded and the challenger lacking visible outside support, the race appears solidly in Democratic hands, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
